segments.text:
GOod Reader, blame not this thyng I beſech thee, which I haue done in this plaine and rude ſort, for the commoditie of the ſimple and vnlearned: whom I did thinke vnable to comprehende in theyr myndes, and to apply vnto their conſciences theſe learned Cōmentaries of this diuine Caluine, vnles they were ſomethyng abbridged and ye expoſitions of the Hebrue wordes, which would haue bene ſomethyng darke in our lā
guage, omitted. Wherfore, as I do profeſſe my ſelfe to bee one of his ſcholers, and do prayſe God for the ſame more then for any earthly matter: ſo do I not of arrogancie alter or chaunge any thing in his writynges. But becauſe I do know right well that if he were alyue hym ſelfe, he would ſuffer all his doings to be applyed to the commoditie of the Church: therfore now whē I do offer his trauayles to the vnlearned of our Engliſh nation, who are deſirous of the ſame, I do ſo preſent them as may be moſt comfortable to their conſcience, and leaſt tedious to ſuch ſimple perſons as are not able to comprehend all his
large and learned diſcourſes. And this abbrydgement do I make but in the two firſt Chapters and in few places beſides: puttyng into print at this preſent, the one halfe of the booke of Daniell, conteynyng the firſt vj. Chapiters, which do treate of the particular hyſtories wrought by God in hys tyme, and therfore ſemeth vnto me farre diuerſe from the latter vj. Chapters: wherin he prophecieth of all thynges that ſhould come vnto the elect people vntill the commyng of Meſsias, and toucheth alſo ſome thynges that be generall vnto all, euen to the end of the world. The which latter part alſo I do meane (by Gods grace) to publiſh for the inſtruction of our nation in theſe obſcure Prophecies, if I can perceaue this former trauayle to be well accepted of the godly, which is my deſire, and whom I do exhorte in the Lord, to read the Scriptures attentyuely, to meditate the ſame diligently, to pray continually.
